subject: Economics
description: Stock exchanges, SEBI, SENSEX/NIFTY, primary vs secondary market

questions.stem: The regulator of INDIA's SECURITIES market is:
questions.explanation: SEBI — statutory body, 1992 Act; HQ Mumbai. Regulates stock exchanges + brokers + mutual funds + IPOs + collective investment schemes. RBI — banks/forex. IRDAI — insurance. PFRDA — pension funds. Present SEBI Chair (2025): Madhabi Puri Buch — first woman SEBI Chair. Securities and Exchange Board of India.
questions.subject: Economics

_fixes.was: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
_fixes.moved_to_explanation: Securities and Exchange Board of India

questions.explanation: SENSEX (Sensitive Index) — 30 large, actively-traded stocks on BSE. Free-float market-cap weighted. Base year 1978-79 = 100. NIFTY 50 (NSE) tracks top 50 stocks. BSE founded 1875 — Asia's oldest stock exchange. NSE founded 1992.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: A COMPANY raising CAPITAL by issuing shares for the FIRST TIME to the public is called:
questions.explanation: IPO — first public share sale. Traded on the 'primary market'. FPO (Follow-on Public Offering) — subsequent issue. OFS (Offer for Sale) — existing shares sold by promoters. Rights issue — shares offered to existing shareholders at discount. Initial Public Offering.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Once an IPO is done, shares are bought and sold on the:
questions.explanation: Primary market — new securities issued. Secondary market — existing securities traded among investors; price discovery happens here. BSE, NSE are secondary markets. MCX, NCDEX are commodity exchanges. stock exchanges like BSE, NSE.
questions.subject: Economics

_fixes.was: Secondary market (stock exchanges like BSE, NSE)

questions.stem: The DEPOSIT INSURANCE LIMIT for bank deposits in India (per depositor per bank) is currently:
questions.explanation: DICGC (Deposit Insurance & Credit Guarantee Corporation, RBI subsidiary) — insures bank deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (raised from ₹1 lakh in 2020). Covers savings/FD/RD/current. PMC Bank crisis prompted the hike.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: A BULL market is a market with:

options.option_text: Falling prices for a sustained period
Rising prices + optimism for a sustained period

questions.explanation: Bull — prices rising, optimism. Bear — prices falling, pessimism. Origin of terms: bulls attack by thrusting HORNS UP (upward motion), bears swipe DOWN with paws. India's longest bull run started post-2003 (Sensex 3,000 → 21,000 by Jan 2008).
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: India's MUTUAL FUND industry is regulated by:
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates Indian MFs. AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) is an industry body. SEBI notifies (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996. Asset Management Companies (AMCs) operate the funds. 'Mutual Funds Sahi Hai' investor-awareness campaign by AMFI since 2017.
